captions.text: Not every deliverable is text. Here a brand manager assigns work on a website to a developer, and ENGANO helps check the result before a reviewer signs it off.
The brand manager signs up and creates a workspace for the web team.
The manager creates the reviewer's account. ENGANO generates the password.
Then posts the assignment: fix the accessibility problems on the landing page, with the page address in the details and a deadline.
The developer signs up and joins with the workspace code.
The assignment is waiting, with its details and deadline. Starting it opens the studio with the title filled in.

The developer pastes the page address. ENGANO opens it in a real browser, scrolls the whole page, tests the links, tries a phone-sized screen and measures accessibility. This takes a while, so we skip ahead.
The result is specific. Every problem says what is wrong and what must be fixed, and the page can't pass until it is.
The developer fixes the page and checks it again. Here a well-built public site stands in for the fixed page.
Now only a minor note remains, so the developer sends the check to the reviewer.
The reviewer sees the task and the page that was checked, with ENGANO's findings and their sources.
They look at the history, add a comment, and approve. If something were wrong they would reject with a note, and the developer would fix and resubmit.
The developer sees the work approved.
The manager finds it in approved drafts, with its full history, without having reviewed anything.
